title: Sack of Constantinople by the Fourth Crusade
summary: After the Fourth Crusade was diverted from Egypt, crusaders broke into Constantinople on 12 April 1204. Three days of looting followed, with citizens massacred and raped, churches desecrated and treasures carried off or melted down. The empire was partitioned, Baldwin of Flanders became Latin emperor, and the Empire of Nicaea retook the city in 1261.

uncertainty.note: Breach on 12 April 1204 from World History Encyclopedia; Fordham dates the sack to 1204 only.

as_recorded.value: on 12 April, the Crusaders attacked the weaker sea walls

where.historical_name: Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire

importance.justification: The sack broke the Byzantine Empire into rival states, created a Latin Empire, and left a lasting break between the Catholic and Orthodox Churches.

audience_note: Describes the killing and rape of civilians and the desecration of churches during the sack of a city.

sources.title: Nicetas Choniates: The Sack of Constantinople (1204)
sources.publisher: Internet History Sourcebooks Project, Fordham University

reviewer_note: Neither opened page gives a death toll, so none is stated; search results offered only unreliable figures. Fordham supplies the diversion of the crusade, the desecration of Hagia Sophia and the Catholic-Orthodox break; World History Encyclopedia supplies the dates, partition and 1261.
